summary: Simon Danczuk’s campaign photo posted on March 22 sparked a backlash after a Twitter user, Neil NW‑Hoopz, highlighted the image as “#oops” while the MP was canvassing in Rochdale. summary: Children from an Afghanistan blast were treated and healed in a NATO hospital in Kabul with the help of nurse Austin. Both children, including Shah Bibi who has learned to paint with a prosthetic arm, have completed treatment and are set to return to their Afghan homes. Despite potential danger from militants, the families hope to reunite with their children as they prepare to return to a war‑torn region.
reference:
The last time Lynette Austin saw the injured Afghan children after an explosion in their village, they were weak, wounded and broken .
When Austin saw  Abdul Wahid and Shah Bibi Tarakhail Friday at Shriners Hospital For Children, she found two cheerful 8-year-olds .
Abdul Wahid was working with his family in the garden of his home in 2013 in a remote, war-torn area when a rocket exploded taking his right leg .
Shah Bibi Tarakhail lost most of her right arm and her right eye when she mistook a discarded grenade outside her home for a rock, and it exploded .

summary:
U.S. ICE agents in New York, Baltimore, Austin, and New Haven uncovered and recovered looted Iraqi artifacts, which were returned to Iraq in a ceremony at its embassy.  
The return underscores Iraq’s commitment to preserving its heritage and signals to ISIS that destruction of cultural sites will not go unanswered.  
The Smithsonian trained Homeland Security investigators in provenance research, illustrated by the 2008 recovery of a limestone statue of Assyrian king Sargon II.
reference:
The move follows a culmination of investigations led by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents .
Lukman Faily, Iraq's ambassador to the U.S., said Monday's ceremony sends a message to Islamic State that Iraq and its allies are committed to rebuilding the country and preserving its cultural heritage .
Among the other items recovered by multi-year investigations are an ancient bronze axe and 21 clay reliefs .

summary: Patsy Byrne, the late Blackadder star, left £20,000 to each of four stepchildren and the rest of her £1.5 million estate to a fifth stepchild. She hadn’t realized she owned about £900,000, so the remainder was to be distributed at her discretion by her stepdaughter. No family dispute emerged, as the will simply allowed flexibility for any future changes.

summary: Line Corp is expanding its popular animal characters—Brown and Cony—into physical stores, games, VR parks, and an upcoming animated film to boost its Line messaging app beyond Asia. The company spun off these merchandising ventures into Line Friends and opened a flagship shop in Seoul’s Gangnam, aiming to build brand awareness even in China where Line is blocked. Analysts see this multi‑channel strategy as a way to generate revenue and potentially re‑launch the app in new markets, despite competition from local messaging giants.

summary: On February 19, an 8th‑grader named Blake suffered a cracked skull, fractured jaw and ear damage after being violently attacked in the Liberty Middle School lunchroom. He spent five days at Children’s Mercy Hospital before being released, while the assailant was arrested and sent to juvenile court. The school district is now implementing bullying‑prevention programs and reviewing the incident.

summary: A 22‑year‑old man named Lockyer threatened a woman with a knife in a Reading canal, saying he would kill her unless she complied, and she escaped by jumping into the water. summary: In 2008 South Los Angeles passed a ban on standalone fast‑food restaurants, yet the ordinance did not restrict strip‑mall or small‑store outlets, allowing unhealthy food to remain accessible. A RAND study found the ban had no measurable effect on diets or obesity rates, which have actually risen in the area. Experts note that a single zoning rule cannot solve obesity; improving access to affordable, healthy foods and encouraging broader lifestyle changes are essential.
reference:
Study shows law only banned construction and expansion of stand-alone fast-food restaurants, which are rare in the area to begin with .
Standalone fast-food restaurants are outnumbered by restaurants in strip malls and convenience stores, which were not restricted by the ban .
Fast food chains opened 17 new outlets in strip shopping centers and food courts in South Los Angeles from 2008 to 2012 .
Almost half of the new food permits were for convenience stores that sell soda and junk food .
